claims.statement: For directional disagreement masses a=P(G0=0,G1=1), b=P(G0=1,G1=0), d=a+b and Delta=a-b, the singleton Poincare currency satisfies E=d-Delta^2=d(1-d)+4ab.
If the s=0 child is a Poincare equality state, W0=0, then W_G(s)=s[W1+(1-s)E]=s(W1+E)-s^2E. If W1+E=0 the parent is itself an equality gate and no quotient is formed.

In the positive-denominator face-contraction branch, the global margin equals [W1*c1+(1-s)E*ell_s]/[W1+(1-s)E], where ell_s=-J_s/[s(1-s)E]. Thus the vanishing selector factor cancels exactly before taking a limit and child slack is retained.

Any common finite cap C on the fixed child margin and the local gluing margin propagates to the full gate all the way to the boundary; boundary blow-up is equivalent to blow-up of the local gluing ratio, not to selector probability shrinkage itself.
